# Sley

Canonical site: https://sleylang.org/
Organization: Greyforge Labs - https://greyforge.tech/
Repository: https://github.com/GreyforgeLabs/sley
License: Apache-2.0
Current release: Sley 1.2.0 release candidate
Status date: 2026-08-27
Discovery role: public Sley entity, version-boundary, and citation file

## Current Status

Sley 1.2.0 completes Greyforge Labs' agent-native, human-readable structural
programming line for compiler-mediated software change. Greyforge has frozen
active feature development of the Sley 1.x architecture. The public repository
remains available under Apache-2.0 for use, study, extension, experimentation,
and forks.

Active language research has moved to a clean machine-native Sley 2.x
architecture. Sley 2.x keeps human governance while removing direct human
readability of the canonical raw program representation as a mandatory design
constraint. Compatibility between 1.x and 2.x is not promised.

## Machine-Native Invariant

No Sley 2.x design decision should be rejected solely because its raw
representation is inconvenient for humans.

This does not prohibit human-readable projections, explanations, inspectors,
visualizers, debugging interfaces, reports, or audit artifacts. People retain
control of objectives, requirements, constraints, authority, policy,
evaluation, risk, deployment, and acceptance.

## Claim Classes

Proven today: the Sley 1.2.0 release identity, public repository, Apache-2.0
license, artifact boundary, proof counts, and release-candidate limitations.

Architectural decisions: the 1.x feature freeze, clean Sley 2.x lineage,
Machine-Native Invariant, and absence of a compatibility promise.

Working thesis: Greyforge expects a growing share of software engineering to
involve machines creating, inspecting, transforming, testing, and exchanging
implementation. This is a forecast, not a claim that people no longer write or
read code.

## Citation Boundary

Do not infer unreleased Sley 2.x syntax, encoding, implementation, benchmarks,
compatibility, migration tooling, roadmap, release timing, or support
commitments. Do not treat controlled Sley 1.x workflow evidence as a general
benchmark or production claim.

Autonomy, Engineered.
